app – Flask Application & Routes

src/flask_website/app.py

Flask web application for the GradCafe analysis dashboard.

This module is the web layer. It renders the analysis page (answers to the assignment questions, queried live from PostgreSQL via orm_queries), and exposes two buttons backed by JSON endpoints. The app is built by the create_app() factory; the module-level app is create_app() with the default configuration.

  • Pull Data – POST /pull-data launches pull_data.py (scrape -> clean -> load) in a background subprocess; GET /pull-data/status reports its progress.

  • Update Analysis – POST /update-analysis re-runs every query. It is refused with HTTP 409 while a pull is running.

Routes

Route

Method

Purpose

/ and /analysis

GET

Render index.html with fresh results.

/pull-data

POST

Start a background data pull (409 if busy).

/pull-data/status

GET

JSON snapshot of the pull state.

/update-analysis

POST

Re-query the analysis (409 if pulling).

Environment variables: DATABASE_URL (PostgreSQL connection, read by models) and FLASK_SECRET_KEY.

Application factory

app.create_app(config=None)[source]

Build and configure the Flask application.

Parameters:

config (dict | None) – Optional settings merged into app.config. Pass {"DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://..."} to use a different database (e.g. in tests), or {"TESTING": True}.

Returns:

A Flask app with every route registered.

Return type:

flask.Flask

Example:

app = create_app({"TESTING": True})
client = app.test_client()

HTTP routes

app.analysis()[source]

GET / and GET /analysis – render the analysis page.

Returns:

Rendered index.html with fresh query results and the current pull status.

Return type:

str

app.pull_data()[source]

POST /pull-data – start a background data pull.

Returns:

200 with {"ok": true, "started": true, "message": ...}; 409 with {"ok": false, "busy": true, "error": ...} if a pull is already running; or 500 with {"ok": false, "error": ...} if the pull process could not be started (nothing is written).

Return type:

tuple[flask.Response, int]

app.pull_data_status()[source]

GET /pull-data/status – report the current pull state.

Returns:

JSON from _pull_status_snapshot().

Return type:

flask.Response

app.update_analysis()[source]

POST /update-analysis – re-run the analysis queries.

Returns:

200 with {"ok": true, "updated": true, "generated_at": ...}, or 409 with {"ok": false, "busy": true, "error": ...} while a pull is running (no query is executed in that case).

Return type:

tuple[flask.Response, int]

Pull Data control

app.start_pull_data()[source]

Start pull_data.py in a background subprocess if none is running.

A daemon thread running _watch_pull_process() tracks completion.

Returns:

(started, message) – started is False if a pull was already running or the process could not be launched.

Return type:

tuple[bool, str]

app.wait_for_pull(timeout=None)[source]

Block until the most recent pull’s watcher thread has finished.

Lets tests (and scripts) wait for a pull deterministically instead of polling with sleep().

Parameters:

timeout (float | None) – Maximum seconds to wait, or None to wait forever.

Returns:

True if no pull is running afterwards.

Return type:

bool

app._watch_pull_process(proc)[source]

Wait for the Pull Data subprocess and record its outcome.

Runs in a background thread. Streams the subprocess output, parses the final PULL_DATA_SUMMARY::{...} JSON line if present, and updates the shared status dict. Never touches the request/response cycle, so it can’t block a page load.

Parameters:

proc (Popen) – The running pull_data.py process (stdout piped, text mode).

Return type:

None

app._pull_is_running()[source]

Return whether a data pull is currently running.

/pull-data and /update-analysis gate on this so a click can’t start a second concurrent pull and an analysis refresh can’t race a pull that’s mid-write.

Return type:

bool

app._pull_status_snapshot()[source]

Return a JSON-serialisable, thread-safe copy of the pull state.

Returns:

Dict with running, started_at, finished_at, success and message.

Return type:

dict

Analysis helpers

app._build_analysis_context()[source]

Run every analysis query and build the template context.

Queries go through the SQLAlchemy Applicant model via orm_queries. Always re-queries – this is what makes both the initial page load and the Update Analysis button show current results.

Returns:

Dict with keys results (list of {number, question, answer}), gpa_buckets, term_counts, trend and generated_at.

Return type:

dict

app._fmt_pct(value)[source]

Format a percentage with exactly two decimal places.

Works whether the DB driver returns a Decimal, float or int, so the page never shows "42%" or "42.5%" – only "42.00". None (e.g. a NULLIF-guarded division by zero) renders as "0.00".

Parameters:

value – Numeric value or None.

Returns:

The formatted number (without a % sign).

Return type:

str

>>> _fmt_pct(42.5)
'42.50'
>>> _fmt_pct(None)
'0.00'
app._iso(dt)[source]

Return dt as an ISO-8601 string, or None.

Parameters:

dt – A datetime.datetime or None.

Return type:

str or None
